why: The roving keyboard order following a surface the player has already left. Before this contract exactly one panel-family element was ever displayed, so `activePanelContainer` could return the first one it found; a crossfade deliberately paints two at once for its duration, and the outgoing one is listed FIRST (`panel`), so without this line the arrow keys walked the screen the player just left for the whole 150ms. Nothing about the visible result changes -- both surfaces are painted either way, the destination still arrives, and every settled-state assertion still passes -- which is why this needs a mutation rather than a screenshot. It is the KEYBOARD half of a rule the stylesheet only covers for the mouse (`.ui-surface--leaving` sets `pointer-events: none`), and it is the reachable half of that rule: `isHiddenWithin`'s sibling check is not, because `--leaving` lands only on the seven surface elements, which are exactly the containers that walk excludes. Scoped to hud.test.ts; expectFailures counts that scoped run only.
